eIDAS2

Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework

Official text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of 11 April 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework (OJ L 2024/1183, 30.4.2024)Tier 1 · primary law

Status
In force as of 27 October 2026
Key dates
3 dated events
Competent authority
not established in this dataset
Sanction ceiling
no amount recorded

In force since 20 May 2024 (Art. 2; OJ L 2024/1183, 30.4.2024); it amends Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and sets no separate application date. Two dated duties follow from the implementing acts under Arts 5a(23) and 5c(6), in force since 24 December 2024: each Member State must provide a European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months, by 24 December 2026 (Art. 5a(1)), and private relying parties that must use strong user authentication — except micro and small enterprises — must accept the wallet at the user's voluntary request within 36 months, by 24 December 2027 (Art. 5f(2)). The first is a duty on Member States, the second a qualified duty on some businesses, not on all. Re-read on 27 Oct 2026 in the Official Journal text retrieved from Cellar.

In short: what you need to know

  • Objective: Secure electronic identification and trust services across the internal market, extended by the European Digital Identity Wallets each Member State must provide and recognise.
  • Who it binds: Member State · Provider of a European Digital Identity Wallet · Relying party · Very large online platform · Gatekeeper · Trust service provider · Web-browser provider · Public authority
  • Who it protects: not established
  • Core obligations: eIDAS2 Art. 5a (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) · eIDAS2 Art. 5b (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) · eIDAS2 Art. 5f (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) · eIDAS2 Art. 12b (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) · eIDAS2 Art. 19a (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) · eIDAS2 Art. 45 (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as replaced) · eIDAS2 Art. 45f (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) key provisions →
  • Key dates: Entry into force 20 May 2024 +2 more dated events →
  • Sanction ceiling: no amount recordedNo ceiling at EU level: Art. 16(2) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as replaced, requires Member States to set administrative fines for trust service providers with a maximum of at least EUR 5 000 000 or, for a legal person, 1 % of worldwide annual turnover if higher. A floor for the national maximum, not a ceiling. enforcement →

When does the eIDAS2 apply? Key dates

Entry into force, application and transposition are different events and are kept apart. A date at month precision is shown as a month rather than invented as a day.

  1. 20 May 2024Entry into forceEntry into force
  2. 24 December 2026Compliance deadlineEach Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet (Art. 5a(1)). A deadline for Member States, not for businesses.
  3. 24 December 2027Compliance deadlinePrivate relying parties that Union or national law or a contract requires to use strong user authentication for online identification must also accept European Digital Identity Wallets, only at the user's voluntary request (Art. 5f(2)). Microenterprises and small enterprises are excluded.What it requires: Where strong user authentication is already required, be able to accept the wallet when a user chooses to use it.

Potentially applicable

activity Providing digital identity services

Under the European Digital Identity framework (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183), each Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the entry into force of the implementing acts under Arts 5a(23) and 5c(6), which entered into force on 24 December 2024. The rule covers the wallet obligation only.

ArticleHeadingBindsApplies
Art. 2 (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended)ScopeApplies to electronic identification schemes notified by a Member State, to European Digital Identity Wallets provided by a Member State and to trust service providers established in the Union (2(1)); it is without prejudice to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (2(4)).not recordedno application date recorded for this article
Art. 3 (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended)DefinitionsPoint (42): 'European Digital Identity Wallet' means an electronic identification means which allows the user to securely store, manage and validate person identification data and electronic attestations of attributes for the purpose of providing them to relying parties and other users of European Digital Identity Wallets, and to sign by means of qualified electronic signatures or to seal by means of qualified electronic seals.not recordedno application date recorded for this article
Art. 5a (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingEuropean Digital Identity WalletsEach Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in Art. 5a(23) and Art. 5c(6) (5a(1)); a wallet is provided directly by a Member State, under a mandate from one, or independently of one but recognised by it (5a(2)). Providers of European Digital Identity Wallets must ensure that users can easily request technical support and report technical problems or other incidents (5a(10)); must neither collect information about the use of the wallet that is not necessary for providing wallet services, nor combine person identification data or other personal data with personal data from other services offered by the provider or from third-party services not necessary for them, unless the user has expressly requested otherwise, and must keep the personal data relating to the wallet logically separate (5a(14)); and Art. 24(2), points (b) and (d) to (h), apply to them mutatis mutandis (5a(20)).Member State · Provider of a European Digital Identity Walletno application date recorded for this article
Art. 5b (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingEuropean Digital Identity Wallet-Relying PartiesA relying party that intends to rely upon European Digital Identity Wallets for the provision of public or private services by means of digital interaction must register in the Member State where it is established, providing at least the information needed to authenticate to wallets, its contact details and the intended use of wallets, including the data it will request from users (5b(1), (2)). Relying parties must not request users to provide data other than that indicated at registration (5b(3)), must inform Member States without delay of changes to it (5b(6)), must identify themselves to the user (5b(8)), are responsible for authenticating and validating the data requested from wallets and must not refuse the use of pseudonyms where Union or national law does not require the user to be identified (5b(9)); an intermediary acting on a relying party's behalf is deemed a relying party (5b(10)). Member States make the registration information publicly available online and provide a common mechanism for identifying and authenticating relying parties (5b(5), (7)).Relying partyno application date recorded for this article
Art. 5f (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingCross-border reliance on European Digital Identity WalletsWhere Member States require electronic identification and authentication to access an online service provided by a public sector body, they must also accept European Digital Identity Wallets (5f(1)). Private relying parties that provide services, with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises, and that are required by Union or national law, or by contractual obligation, to use strong user authentication for online identification must also accept wallets, no later than 36 months from the entry into force of the implementing acts under Arts 5a(23) and 5c(6) and only upon the user's voluntary request (5f(2)); the size test is an exemption, so medium-sized enterprises are covered. Providers of very large online platforms that require user authentication for access to online services must also accept and facilitate the use of wallets, only upon the user's voluntary request and for the minimum data necessary (5f(3)).Member State · Relying party · Very large online platformno application date recorded for this article
Art. 12b (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingAccess to hardware and software featuresWhere providers of European Digital Identity Wallets and issuers of notified electronic identification means that act in a commercial or professional capacity, and use core platform services as defined in Art. 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 to provide wallet services and electronic identification means to end-users, are business users as defined in Art. 2, point (21), of that Regulation, gatekeepers must in particular allow them effective interoperability with, and, for the purposes of interoperability, access to, the same operating system, hardware or software features, free of charge and regardless of whether those features are part of the operating system, are available to or are used by the gatekeeper itself. The Article is without prejudice to Art. 5a(14).Gatekeeperno application date recorded for this article
Art. 19a (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingRequirements for non-qualified trust service providersA non-qualified trust service provider providing non-qualified trust services must have appropriate policies and take corresponding measures to manage legal, business, operational and other direct or indirect risks to the service, including at least measures on registration and onboarding procedures, procedural or administrative checks and the management and implementation of trust services, notwithstanding Art. 21 of Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (19a(1)(a)); and must notify the supervisory body, the identifiable affected individuals, the public if it is of public interest and, where applicable, other competent authorities, of any security breach or disruption that has a significant impact on the service or the personal data in it, without undue delay and in any case no later than 24 hours after becoming aware (19a(1)(b)). Qualified trust service providers are bound by Art. 24(2), not by this Article.Trust service providerno application date recorded for this article
Art. 45 (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as replaced) load-bearingRequirements for qualified certificates for website authenticationQualified certificates for website authentication must meet the requirements of Annex IV (45(1)). They must be recognised by providers of web-browsers, who must ensure that the identity data attested in the certificate and additional attested attributes are displayed in a user-friendly manner and must ensure support and interoperability with those certificates; microenterprises and small enterprises are excepted during the first five years of operating as providers of web-browsing services (45(1a)). Qualified certificates for website authentication are not subject to any mandatory requirements other than those of paragraph 1 (45(1b)).Web-browser providerno application date recorded for this article
Art. 45f (of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as inserted) load-bearingRequirements for electronic attestation of attributes issued by or on behalf of a public sector body responsible for an authentic sourcePublic sector bodies issuing electronic attestations of attributes under this Article must provide an interface with European Digital Identity Wallets provided in accordance with Art. 5a (45f(8)). The Member State where such bodies are established must ensure that they meet a level of reliability and trustworthiness equivalent to qualified trust service providers under Art. 24 (45f(2)), and must notify them to the Commission with a conformity assessment report (45f(3)). An attestation issued by or on behalf of such a body must meet Annex VII and the conditions of paragraph 1, including a qualified certificate supporting the body's qualified electronic signature or seal (45f(1)); once revoked it loses its validity and its status is not reverted (45f(4)). 'Public sector body' in this Regulation includes a private entity mandated by a public authority to provide public services, when acting under that mandate (Art. 3, point (7)).Public authority · Member Stateno application date recorded for this article

2 Primary law
Primary law law

Under eIDAS2 each Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the entry into force of the implementing acts under Articles 5a(23) and 5c(6) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014; those acts entered into force on 24 December 2024, which puts the deadline at 24 December 2026.

Tier 1 · primary law states this

Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of 11 April 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework (OJ L 2024/1183, 30.4.2024) — Publications Office of the European Union (Cellar) 30 April 2024 Art. 1, inserting Art. 5a(1) into Regulation (EU) No 910/2014

Primary law law

From 24 December 2027, private relying parties that Union or national law or a contract requires to use strong user authentication for online identification must also accept European Digital Identity Wallets, but only at the user's voluntary request; microenterprises and small enterprises are excluded.

Tier 1 · primary law states this

Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of 11 April 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework (OJ L 2024/1183, 30.4.2024) — Publications Office of the European Union (Cellar) 30 April 2024 Art. 1, inserting Art. 5f(2) into Regulation (EU) No 910/2014: 'with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises'; 'no later than 36 months from the date of entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in Article 5a(23) and Article 5c(6) and only upon the voluntary request of the user'

Tier 1 · primary law supports in part

Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2977 of 28 November 2024 as regards person identification data and electronic attestations of attributes issued to European Digital Identity Wallets — EUR-Lex 4 December 2024 OJ L, 2024/2977, 4.12.2024; entry into force on the twentieth day following publication (24 December 2024)

How does the eIDAS2 interact with other EU laws?

2 recorded interactions with other instruments — each with a direction, the provisions that carry it and its own sources. Direction is preserved as recorded: an instrument that amends another is not the same as one amended by it.

eIDAS2 Amends eIDAS Regulation

eIDAS2 amends the eIDAS Regulation: among other changes, it replaces its subject matter, which now includes the European Digital Identity Wallets, and its first five definitions, and inserts a governance chapter with the supervisory bodies of Art. 46b.
